q48231.dateNote: His birth date is not known; about 1925.

cur-fossil-melka-kunture.dateNote: In 1963 the engineer Gérard Dekker found stone tools along the upper Awash River, south of Addis Ababa. Digs since have found tools and early human bones from about 1.7 million years ago on.
cur-fossil-melka-kunture.summary: A string of early human camps on the upper Awash River in Ethiopia, with tools and bones.

cur-fossil-kanapoi.dateNote: In 1965 a Harvard team led by Bryan Patterson found an arm bone here, west of Lake Turkana in Kenya. In 1994 Meave Leakey's team found more, and named Australopithecus anamensis. It is about 4.2 million years old.
cur-fossil-kanapoi.summary: Home of Australopithecus anamensis, one of the oldest known australopiths.

cur-fossil-omo.dateNote: In 1967 Richard Leakey's team found two skulls by the Omo River in southern Ethiopia. Ash above them gives an age of at least 233,000 years (0.23 million years): among the oldest of our own kind.

cur-fossil-lomekwi.dateNote: In 2011 a team took a wrong turn west of Lake Turkana, Kenya, and found stone tools 3.3 million years old — older than any human fossil of our genus Homo.

cur-find-lothagam-north.dateNote: Near Lake Turkana, Kenya, herders built eastern Africa's earliest known monumental cemetery about 5,000 years ago: a platform with stone pillars over hundreds of burials (Hildebrand et al., PNAS, 2018).
